target_customer: Consumers on Facebook and online communities; merchants as revenue source
problem: People discussed products inside communities but had no easy way to discover and buy them there. Mertado embedded shopping and Facebook based recommendations.
business_model: affiliate and commerce commission on products sold

founders.name: Vijay Chittoor
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he helped build early semantic search at Kosmix.

founders.name: Mehul Shah
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, later at Groupon Goods and Blueshift.

founders.name: Rajiv Bhat
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Facebook Connect integration, a recommendation engine and an embeddable shopping widget, built by two ex-Kosmix engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Dependent on Facebook distribution and merchant feeds, with little lock-in and easy imitation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Groupon bought the company in January 2012 and shut the product on 28 February 2012 to fold it into Groupon Goods.

market_need_then: Social commerce was rising in 2010 as Facebook Connect spread and shoppers followed recommendations in communities. Direct evidence of demand for Mertado specifically was not found.

branding.domain_note: mertado.com now redirects to a third party site about the domain, so the original site is dead.
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found. A branding search only returned unrelated Mercado brands, suggesting confusion with the Spanish word for market.

brand_strength.rationale: Forgettable and easily confused with Mercado names; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Mertado raised a 2.3 million dollar Series A in September 2011 led by Rustic Canyon, then was bought by Groupon four months later in January 2012, and the product closed on 28 February 2012. The team joined Groupon Goods, which fits a soft landing for the team rather than a standalone growth story. Traction metrics are not public, so the quality of the exit is unclear.
notes: Funding total of 2.3M is the same figure in TechCrunch and SoCalTech; Seedtable also lists it. The investor Y Combinator is named by TechCrunch but the YC deal terms are not a round. One source (Finsmes) says Spring 2010 batch; YC page says Winter 2010. Competitor sources dated near the April 2010 launch were not found (Wanelo launched Oct 2010, after the batch), so the list is empty. Acquihire label is inferred from the product shutdown and Groupon Goods roles, not stated by a source.
